messages:
ash: Heads-up — after last night's burst in eu-west we saw another high-tier customer hit tail latency because of cross-tenant KV-cache churn. Thinking we should seriously consider segmented pools for SLA customers rather than just nicer routing rules. :thinking:

maria: Do you mean physical separation (dedicated pools) or logical (taints/labels + scheduler quotas)? physical will kill utilization, logical might not guarantee isolation under noise.

ash: Prefer physical for the highest SLA (gold) — small dedicated fleets per region. For silver we could use soft isolation (taints + preemption thresholds) and fallback to lower-cost shared. Tradeoff: cost vs predictable latency.

ben: Also worth considering a hybrid burst model — reserved slots that sit idle but can be preempted by infra for other tenants when unused, and autoscaled up for burst windows. That keeps committed cost lower than 24/7 dedicated.

june: How would we enforce network/QoS boundaries? GPU contention is one thing but network saturation + NFS metadata storms also cause tail spikes. Are we comfortable with cross-region replication for stateful caches?

ash: Good point — proposal sketch below for ops to review. Looking for feedback on routing constraints, autoscale behavior, and eviction semantics before we draft RFC.

ash: ```
# sketch: pool config
{
  "pool_name": "gold-eu-west-2",
  "mode": "dedicated",
  "min_nodes": 2,
  "max_nodes": 8,
  "cpu_label": "gpu:a100",
  "network_qos": "high",
  "kv_cache": "local-ssd:enabled",
  "preemptible": false
}
```

maria: That looks reasonable for gold. For silver, I would add: ``"preemptible": true, "eviction_grace": 120`` and a routing policy that prefers silver->shared only if cold-cache penalty is acceptable.

ben: One operational concern: dedicated pools fragment capacity and increase number of autoscale groups. That's complexity in our provisioning pipeline and in cost forecasting. We need a clear forecast metric: cost per p95 reduction.

june: Can we instrument a metric that ties a customer’s p95 jump to cross-tenant scheduling events? Like correlate preemption_count + KV-cache-evictions with p95 delta. If we can show causality we can justify dedicated spend.

ops-bot: Alert summary (auto): GPU_preemptions: 3.4% (24h), tail_latency_p95_for_gold: +120ms (6h window), shared_pool_utilization_eu-west-2: 78% :warning: Dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/infra/pools?region=eu-west-2

ash: Exactly, ops-bot numbers are the data we need. Maria — can you run a query to produce per-customer correlation for the last 7 days? Ben/june — please sketch cost model for 1 dedicated 8xA100 pool in eu-west-2 vs leaving in shared with QoS and burst credits.

maria: On it. I can produce the correlation + a flamegraph for cache evictions. Will post results here by EOD.

ben: I'll model costs and include a sensitivity sweep (utilization 30-90%). Will also add a hybrid option where we keep a small dedicated pool + burstable shared overlay.

june: I'll check network QoS options with cloud network team and verify whether we can reserve throughput for the pool (or use separate NICs/placement groups).

ash: If we converge, next step is an RFC with concrete numbers + rollout plan: labeling, autoscale policies, cost allocation, and a safe fallback (route to lower-tier model) for overload. Thanks — would love quick takes if anyone else sees a blocker. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: if we create dedicated pools we'll need a new quota flow for sales to request capacity. Existing quota service: https://internal/redwood/quota (ticketing required).

maria: One quick gotcha — some enterprise customers require private deployment. For them dedicated pools are easier (and cheaper at scale) because we don't pay cloud egress for cross-tenant isolation. Include that in the RFC.

ben: Agree. Also adding recommendation: automated nightly consolidation job to reclaim underutilized dedicated pools (scale-to-zero with warm images) to limit wasted spend.

ash: Great. I'll compile notes and open an RFC draft tomorrow with a cost appendix and the correlation graphs. If anyone has hard constraints I should call out, DM me.

june: ping if you want me to join the RFC review — I can bring network and scheduler constraints.

ash: Thanks all.
